record.paper_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
record.original_question: How should branch-cut cosmology be reformulated quantum mechanically, rather than only through leading-order classical equations of motion, so that the intrinsically quantum evolutionary domain near the primordial transition is described more faithfully?

evidence.quote: A quantum approach, more in line with the nature of this evolutionary domain, following a recent proposal Zen Vasconcellos et al. (2021a), is under investigation.

Evidently, most of these questions should not be limited to a classical description of the evolutionary universe, as their nature is intrinsically quantum. These topics are presently under investigation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the framework of "branch-cut cosmology," in which the cosmological scale factor a(t) of a Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker-type universe is analytically continued to a multi-valued complex function defined on a Riemann surface with a branch cut, so that the classical primordial singularity is replaced by a finite branch-cut transition region connecting a contracting pre-bounce sheet to an expanding post-bounce sheet. At leading order, the dynamics of the (complexified) scale factor are governed by classical Einstein-type equations of motion obtained from a Hořava–Lifshitz-style gravitational action (with higher spatial-derivative curvature terms) coupled, possibly, to a scalar inflaton field.

Provide a fully quantum-mechanical reformulation of this model. Concretely:

1. Starting from a Hořava–Lifshitz gravitational Lagrangian density coupled to matter, perform an ADM (Arnowitt–Deser–Misner) decomposition adapted to the branch-cut geometry and derive the corresponding Hamiltonian constraint H = 0 in which the dynamical variable is the complex branch-cut scale factor β(t) and its conjugate momentum π_β.

2. Promote β and π_β to operators satisfying canonical commutation relations, choose an operator-ordering prescription (with explicit ordering parameters), and obtain the resulting Wheeler–DeWitt-type equation Ĥ Ψ(β) = 0 — equivalently, a Schrödinger-type equation with a (generically non-linear) effective potential — governing the wave function Ψ of the universe on the branch-cut Riemann surface.

3. Specify boundary/matching conditions for Ψ across the branch cut connecting the contracting and expanding sheets, and demonstrate that the resulting quantum evolution describes a non-singular quantum transition (a "quantum leap") between the two phases consistent with the Bekenstein entropy bound.

4. Show that, in an appropriate semiclassical/WKB limit, the quantum description reduces to the leading-order classical branch-cut equations of motion, and analyze quantum corrections to observables in the primordial transition region.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works (2022–2024) by Hess, Zen Vasconcellos, Hadjimichef, Bodmann, de Freitas Pacheco and collaborators have developed Wheeler–DeWitt quantum formulations of branch-cut cosmology: a topological canonical quantum-mechanics approach (Astron. Nachr. 2023; arXiv:2212.03832), a Wheeler–DeWitt approach with operator-ordering parameters (Universe 9 (2023) 278), a non-commutative Wheeler–DeWitt extension (Universe 9 (2023) 428), and applications to primordial gravitational waves (arXiv:2401.06902). These provide concrete partial quantum reformulations along the lines requested, although a complete, fully observationally tested quantum theory of the branch-cut transition is still under development.

status_evidence.snippet: Topological canonical quantum-mechanics approach to branch-cut cosmology.

status_evidence.title: A Wheeler–DeWitt Quantum Approach to the Branch-Cut Gravitation with Ordering Parameters
status_evidence.snippet: Wheeler–DeWitt equation for branch-cut cosmology with explicit operator-ordering parameters, yielding a Schrödinger-type equation with nonlinear potential.
status_evidence.claim: A Wheeler–DeWitt quantum formulation with ordering parameters has been constructed.

status_evidence.title: A Wheeler–DeWitt Non-Commutative Quantum Approach to the Branch-Cut Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Non-commutative extension of the Wheeler–DeWitt quantization of branch-cut gravity.
status_evidence.claim: Non-commutative quantum extensions of the model exist.

status_evidence.title: Primordial gravitational waves in Wheeler-DeWitt non-commutative linearized branch-cut quantum gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Application of the Wheeler–DeWitt branch-cut quantum gravity to primordial gravitational waves.
status_evidence.claim: Observational/phenomenological consequences of the quantum reformulation are being investigated.
